title: The 20% Fee Plan Is Gone the Next Day. But the Oil Market Show Goes On
part1:
This was a dramatic turn of events in the oil market over two days.

First, on July 13, Mr. Trump made a post. It proposed seeking a 20 percent payment for all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz, as the cost of the United States providing safety and security.

However, at that point, no details had been given about who would pay, how the payment would be calculated, or how it would be collected. A large number had appeared, but the system behind it had not yet been designed.

On the same day, Brent futures rose by $7.29 and settled at $83.30 a barrel. This was a 9.59 percent rise from the previous day. Reuters linked the rise to concerns about a U.S. sea blockade of Iran, said to begin the next day, and about energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
part2:
What matters here is the order of events in time. The events of the next day came after the July 13 settlement price had been released.

On July 14, Mr. Trump posted that he was withdrawing the 20 percent fee and replacing it with trade and investment deals between the Gulf states and the United States. He also told reporters that he believed no one should charge a fee to ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The fee plan that appeared the day before was replaced by a different matter the next day.

The market's movement also looked like a change of scene. After the announcement of the withdrawal and replacement, Brent futures temporarily narrowed their gains. But before long, they returned to a high level close to where they had been before the announcement. At the time the article was published, they were up about 2.6 percent and above $85 a barrel.
part3:
On the other hand, daily data showed that the July 14 settlement price was $84.73. It was up $1.43 from the previous day, a rise of 1.7 percent. The price in the breaking news and the final price for the day looked slightly different.

The day's price movement reflected not only the withdrawal announcement, but also attacks by the United States and Iran, the sea blockade, and concerns about tanker safety. So this was not a simple story in which the market suddenly reached its end when the fee plan disappeared. It was a two-day period in which statements, ships, attacks, and prices changed the scene one after another on the same stage.
in_one_line: Oil prices stayed high even after Trump dropped the proposed 20% Strait of Hormuz fee the next day.
